title: Calibration test 1b: same test, after correcting for how each scan counts synapses
written: 2026-11-03T02:25Z, AFTER seeing test 1a (Maxime: MN9 almost silent; Hagrid: runaway activity) and BEFORE any 1b run. This is a new, stated hypothesis, not a re-run until it passes.
hypothesis: Test 1a used the published strength per synapse (0.275 mV), which was set on the FlyWire brain. The three scans count synapses very differently: a typical neuron receives a median of 104 synapses (strong connections) in FlyWire, 38 in Maxime's scan and 206 in Hagrid's. If that counting difference is why 1a failed, then giving each synapse a strength scaled to make a typical neuron's total input match FlyWire should make both flies pass.
rule: Strength per synapse = 0.275 mV x (FlyWire median input per neuron / this fly's median input per neuron), counting connections of 5+ synapses in each. Fixed from anatomy alone, before any run; never adjusted to the MN9 result.
criteria: Exactly the same rules C1-C5 and pass rule as test 1a.
if_it_fails: Then synapse counting alone does not explain the failure, and that fly's taste-to-tongue wiring is reported as not reproducing the real fly.
